Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Bridgeway deployment evidence & acceptance asks

Hi Mike / NetOps team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, we want to collect the minimal set of evidence items so Redwood engineering and our security reviewers can sign off on the Bridgeway attachment for the private deployment. Below is the consolidated ask from the call — could you confirm ETA for each item by end of week?

Action items (EdgeBridge / Acme NetOps):
- Share the current network attachment diagram (L2/3) annotated with the placement of the Bridgeway appliance and the path to the tenant egress gateway.
- Export the NAT / SNAT table for the interface facing customer control-plane (CSV is fine).
- Provide the ACLs applied at the transit switch and any hairpin rules that would affect KV cache traffic.
- Confirm MTU and any jumbo frame requirements between racks.
- Attach a signed copy of the deployment checklist after the first staging run.

I attached the reference diagram we used in the call and a starter checklist for convenience. Internally I'll loop in ops to validate the NAT table format.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridgeway-deploy-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)

Date: 2026-05-17T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeway deployment evidence & acceptance asks

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and a few attachments: bridgeway-diagram-v1.pdf (updated labels), nat table export, and a first-pass checklist with our internal stamps.

Status:
- Diagram: attached (updated portlabels and VLAN IDs). ETA: done (see attachment).
- NAT/SNAT: attached CSV. Note that we collapse ephemeral ports for the 10.42.0.0/16 tenant pool behind the Bridgeway SNAT due to upstream provider constraints.
- ACLs: we do have an explicit deny for cross-tenant forwarding on the switch (config excerpt included in the diagram notes).
- MTU: default 1500 on the fabric; we can enable 9000 on request but need staging window.
- Deployment checklist: attached with our staging sign-off for the pilot on May 20.

We do have one ask from our side: can Redwood confirm whether the control-plane heartbeat will keep persistent TCP connections to the Bridgeway appliance or whether you prefer short-lived RPCs? That affects whether we keep NAT mappings open for long flows.

Attachment: bridgeway-diagram-v1.pdf (PDF - annotated)
Attachment: bridgeway-nat-table.csv (CSV)
Attachment: bridgeway-deploy-checklist.xlsx (XLSX - EdgeBridge staging stamp)

Best,
Mike Turner
Director, Integrations
EdgeBridge Inc.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Mike Turner <mike@edgebridge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeway deployment evidence & acceptance asks

Mike — thanks for the attachments, very helpful. A few clarifications from the runtime/ops side:

1) Heartbeat / connection model:
- For Redwood Dedicated/Private control-plane we prefer long-lived TLS connections for KV cache performance (reduces cold fetches, preserves session affinity). If EdgeBridge will SNAT those connections, please confirm that NAT timeouts are configurable or that you can send occasional keepalives to maintain mappings.

2) NAT table notes:
- The CSV looks good; two ask items: include the source port ranges used by our runtime nodes (we expect ephemeral 30000-32767 by default in our images) and mark which entries are static vs ephemeral. That helps ops reconcile with provider NAT limits.

3) ACL / hairpin behavior:
- We saw in the diagram that intra-rack hairpin is blocked by default. For the pilot we need an exception for the tenant staging pod (10.42.11.0/24) to reach the Bridgeway management endpoint for health checks. Please indicate how you want that exception expressed (ACL rule id or interface-based).

4) Cutover window:
- Requesting a 2-hour staging window on May 20, 02:00-04:00 UTC for enabling jumbo frames and validating traffic. If jumbo frames are not necessary for the pilot, we can skip that change.

I'll draft a short acceptance checklist once we get the updated NAT CSV.

--
Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick compliance and ops checklist from my side before we mark this as accepted for the pilot:

Compliance/ops acceptance checklist (short):
- Updated diagram with VLANs and interface IDs (received) - OK
- NAT/SNAT table with static/ephemeral columns (EdgeBridge to update) - pending
- ACL exception documented with rule id or interface mapping (EdgeBridge to confirm) - pending
- Reference Drive folder with signed checklist and deploy artifacts (EdgeBridge provided link) - OK
- Signed MOU for limited staging access (legal copied separately) - pending

Please drop the updated NAT CSV and ACL rule id here when ready. Per Jonas, the NAT timeout / keepalive behavior is the critical item for long-lived control-plane connections; if EdgeBridge can expose the timeout settings or agree to keepalives, we can proceed with the May 20 staging window contingent on legal sign-off for the temporary access.

I'll open a short internal ticket to track the outstanding items and will post the ticket ID here.

--
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
